findings.reason: §21 leans on the single-owner claim to justify reusing the path resolver instead of adding one; correcting it means either deriving `delivered_reports`' root from the owner or qualifying the claim, which changes §21's text.
findings.text: `delivered_reports` builds `reports_dir() / project / "plan-review" / plan_slug` while §21 declares `review_report_directory` (line 791) the single owner of that layout and derives the new snapshot path from it; two spellings of one layout in one file drift when the layout moves, and §21's reuse justification rests on an ownership claim that is not true as written — the owner to extend is `review_report_directory` at reckon/crew/plan_review.py:791, and the duplicate to fold is the root at line 866

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16's `section_prose` on `reckon/_plan_html.py` is one function hiding span discovery, protected-span subtraction, entity decoding and tag stripping behind an ordered `(identity, prose)` sequence, and §22 extends `_review_coverage` (a test, a locator and a declaration comparison behind the one predicate) rather than spreading wrappers over it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §21 names `review_report_directory` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:791) "the one owner of the report-directory layout" and adds "no second spelling of the layout", but `delivered_reports` re-spells the same layout at reckon/crew/plan_review.py:866, so the owner §21 relies on for its snapshot path is not single.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds the public `section_prose` and offsets it against the interim public `strip_tags` it privatises (net +1 to the family over the section, stated in its own text), §22 adds `plan_review_settings` and retires `plan_review_settle_seconds` in the same change (net 0) and reuses the `plan-review-missing` refusal family with the uncovered units in its detail (no refusal family added), and §23 adds the public `store_delivered_reviews` while stating its only retirement is routing's uncounted private copy- each section accounts for its surface in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every mechanism the four sections extend is named and present: `_section_digests`, `_review_coverage`/`_fingerprint_forms`, `plan_review_path`, `review_report_directory`, `write_review_sidecar`, `store_delivered_report`/`delivered_reports` in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, `plan_review_settle_seconds` and its §7 schema-exclusion path in `reckon/flight.py:684`/`:322`/`:863`, and `section_record_id`/`structured_section_spans`/`strip_tags` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`; §22's word-level edit share has no prior helper in the tree (no `difflib`/`SequenceMatcher`/change-ratio use exists), so nothing is rebuilt.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 deletes the interim `_prose_slices` rather than leaving it a delegator (grep-enforced in its done-when) and folds `_strip_tags` back to private, and §23 hoists `routing._store_delivered_plan_review` to `plan_review.store_delivered_reviews` and retires the routing copy rather than layering a second store step over it.
